question.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=4$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $-5$ | $-\sqrt{2}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=4.$ Do not round the answer.

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=4}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))=f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=4$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=4} & =f(4){g}^{′}(4)+g(4){f}^{′}(4) \\  & =(\sqrt{2})(\frac{1}{2})+(-5)(-\sqrt{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+5\sqrt{2} \\  & =\frac{11\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
